source_text: CAPUT DECIMUM OCTAVUM, De sanctificatione et bonis operibus. Sanctificatio sive renovatio fidelium et BONA OPERA sunt actiones hominum conversorum per operationem Spiritus Sancti ex vera fide secundum normam legis divinae praestitae, quibus singulis momentis in ipsis peccatum mortificatur et imago Dei renovatur ad obedientiam atque honorem Deo deferendum. Renovatio a regeneratione differt: per regenerationem filii Dei efficimur; per renovationem filii Dei declaramur. Illa mutatio status; haec qualitatum.
english: CHAPTER EIGHTEEN. On sanctification and good works.

Sanctification or renewal of believers and GOOD WORKS are actions of the converted performed by the Holy Spirit's operation from true faith according to the norm of divine law, by which moment by moment sin is mortified in them and God's image renewed unto obedience and honor to God.
Renewal differs from regeneration: by regeneration we are made God's children; by renewal we are declared such. The one changes state; the other qualities.

source_text: Efficiens principalis est Spiritus Sanctus (Rom. 8:14; Ezek. 36:26-27). Proxima et secundaria causa est vera fides per charitatem efficax (Gal. 5:6). Forma bonorum operum posita est in congruentia cum lege Dei—peccatum est anomia, bonum opus isonomia. Quia tamen opera fidelium imperfecta sunt, per fidem in Christum defectus supplentur et Christus fide apprehensus suam iustitiam nostram facit, ut opera Deo placeant (Gen. 4:4; Heb. 11:4).
english: The principal efficient cause is the Holy Spirit; the proximate secondary cause is true faith working through love.

The form of good works lies in conformity to God's law—sin is lawlessness, a good work is law-keeping. Yet because believers' works are imperfect, defects are supplied through faith in Christ, and Christ apprehended by faith makes His righteousness ours so that the works please God.

source_text: Fines: propter Deum obedientia et honor; propter nos ipsos ut vocationem confirmemus; propter proximum ut charitatis officiis sublevemus nec scandala simus. De necessitate: bona opera non sunt necessaria ad iustificationem tanquam causa, sed necessaria sunt in iustificatis tanquam fructus et via vitae Christianae—contra Pontificios qui ea in iustificationem ingerunt.
english: Ends: toward God—obedience and honor; toward ourselves—confirming our calling; toward the neighbor—relieving by love's duties and avoiding scandal.

On necessity: good works are not necessary to justification as a cause, but are necessary in the justified as fruit and the Christian way of life—against those who thrust them into justification itself.

source_text: VII. De perfectione: asserimus bona sanctorum opera in hac vita non esse perfecta ad mensuram legis. VIII. Ea imperfectio frequentissime ratione partium, semper vero ratione graduum. Opus est quotidiana remissione; nemo prior dedit Deo ut retribuatur ei. Meritum condignum et congruum repudiandum; Deus coronat in nobis sua dona, non nostra merita (Augustine).
english: VII–VIII. On perfection: we assert that the saints' good works in this life are not perfect by the law's measure. That imperfection appears often as to parts, always as to degrees.
Daily remission is needed; no one first gave to God so as to be repaid. Condign and congruent merit are to be rejected; God crowns His own gifts in us, not our merits.

source_text: 1. Bonorum operum studium necessario includit sui ipsius abnegationem et crucis tolerantiam. 2. Quae Christianis facienda sint, lex Dei perfecte ostendit tanquam divina regula et canon; Christus exemplar. Sine vera Dei notitia ferri nequeunt. CAPUT DECIMUM NONUM sequitur, De libertate Christiana.
english: 1. Zeal for good works necessarily includes self-denial and bearing the cross. 2. What Christians must do, God's law perfectly shows as divine rule and canon; Christ is the pattern. Without true knowledge of God they cannot be borne.
CHAPTER NINETEEN follows, On Christian liberty.
